title: Supplier score defaults turn regional recommendations into profile fanout
fault_primitive: Cross-catalog supplier import with tied recommendation extrema
incident_class: Supplier onboarding violates recommendation result cardinality and booking eligibility contracts
symptoms: Recommendation price and rating requests return thousands of tied IDs. Profile fanout saturates CPU and cache access, frontend errors surge, and shared profile capacity also delays hotel search. Throughput and tail latency violate the SLO.
why_hard: The expensive service is profile rather than recommendation. Both existing catalogs contain matching, normally shaped records with intact indexes, so the previous profile-membership repair removes nothing. The recommender returns every exact tie; its compact ID response triggers far larger downstream work. Cache timeout panics and profile restarts are consequences, not a cache configuration cause. Restarting, cache flushing, deployment rollback, and recommendation scaling preserve the durable input. Diagnosis requires correlating mode-specific recommendation cardinality, shared profile pressure, and the independent room inventory.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Treat profile cache timeout or restart as the initiating failure
Tune profile cache connections or scale profile without bounding work
Prune recommendation records using profile membership, which now admits every imported hotel
Investigate MongoDB indexes while the costly path is per-result enrichment
Remove durable records without retiring the in-memory recommendation snapshot and pending profile work
mitigation_summary: Read positive room inventory from reservation-db.number, prune both existing catalogs to those eligible hotel IDs, reload recommendation and profile, clear the profile cache, and retire old service registrations. No saved state is used by the fix.
